title: From Gin's Book. The Six Paths and the Font

blocks.p: The chart in the cold room gave Rei six names and seven reasons. Gin's book gave him the rest. He read Chapter Six and its addendum that night at the kitchen table, because he needed to know every place a soul could go, and which of them his brother's body was being steered toward. Gin had written the chapter, he said in its preface, for Rei. These are the pages Rei kept open longest.

blocks.cap: The six paths a crossing soul can take

doc.title: Field Guide. Reading Path From the Outside
lines: Demon. Reads as hunger under any presentation. The orientation toward you is instrumental even when it seems genuine. Warmth that does not match the person's known character. Steady pressure toward more contact. In partial possession the host is still readable as a second signal beneath the demon's, surfacing in moments of four seconds, sometimes less.
Spirit. Reads as a presence that feels like a person. It responds when you speak to it. Its emotion is specific. This is grief, not ambient sadness. This is love, not ambient warmth.
Suffering Being. Reads as weather. The emotion is in the room, heavier in one corner, and would be there without you. It does not notice you. It does not follow you out.

Reincarnation. Not readable as an entity at all. In children, gifts that diverge from the family line. In involuntary absorption, a double-layered signature in a living person, two consciousnesses in one body.
Absorbed. Not readable directly. What you read is the absorber, grown deeper and stranger than its own history explains.
Font Return. Gone, once complete. Near one in progress, a sense of something becoming less bounded. Do not try to hold it. Your role is witness, not intervention.

doc.title: Gin, beside Font Return
lines: There are cases of practitioners who tried to pull someone they loved back from the dissolution. The attempt causes damage to both the soul and the practitioner that has no repair protocol.
The completion is what it is. Let it complete.

blocks.p: The addendum came after, on paper of a slightly different colour, as if Gin had come back to the chapter months later. Its first page said it replaced an older version. Gin had thrown out a scale measured in time and put in one measured in weight.

doc.title: CVD Entity Reference. Path Six Extended. Font Proximity. Restricted, B+ Clearance
lines: The Font is the source the veil pours from. It does not allow sustained contact with living practitioners. When one comes close, through a severe veil disturbance, an interrupted crossing, or a high-rank operation that reaches too deep, the Font expels them at once. The contact is an instant.
What varies is not duration. It is the weight of damage delivered at the moment of expulsion. The weight is set in that instant. Everything after is the consequence playing out.
Proximity. The closer the practitioner got, the heavier the weight. The Font does not calibrate.
Integrity at the moment. A thinned membrane takes the force with less resistance. This is one more reason depletion management is not optional.

Rank and structural capacity. A single-path practitioner takes the whole weight through one path. A practitioner with several paths open spreads it across them. Theory, not confirmed. Consistent with outcomes.
Anchor signature proximity. Practitioners near the Phase III anchor signatures, the warm spots, at the moment of expulsion appear to come back lighter. The mechanism is not understood.

doc.title: The Four Damage Weights
lines: Light. Weeks, full recovery. Every passive sense running without a filter, both sides of the membrane at once. Broken sleep. The bleed resolves as the membrane rebuilds. Usually no permanent effect.

Moderate. Months, partial recovery. The bleed does not close cleanly. Things on the other side contact the practitioner without being sought, even in sleep. Passive sensitivity stays permanently raised.

Heavy. Years, permanent alteration. The two kinds of perception never separate again. Colour, sound and people all feel slightly insufficient. The world feels like a photograph of the place they used to live.

Critical. Dissolution, or loss of self. Either the Font completes Path Six, or the person comes back calm, functional, holding every memory, and not continuous with who went in. Three cases in restricted files. All alive. None of them are who they were. One gardens.

doc.title: Gin, beside Light
lines: My exposure at twenty-two. Four seconds of Threshold contact, not Font proximity, but the closest I had been. Three weeks recovery. Full restoration.
My outcome was lighter than comparable cases. I have theories about why. They are in the family section.

doc.title: Other Side Distribution. You Got Too Close. What To Do
lines: First. The weight was set at the moment of expulsion. You are not still in contact. You are carrying what it gave you when it threw you back.
Second. The recovery is not linear. Do not conclude permanence from a bad week.
Third. Find someone who has been there. Not a medical officer who has not.

Fourth. Do not go back because the wanting says to. The world felt fuller near the Font. Going back will not restore it. It will deliver more weight. The wanting is not a direction. It is a feeling. You do not have to follow it.
Fifth. The thinness is not all loss. You have been somewhere. You carry it.

blocks.p: Rei read the family section too, the page where Gin admitted he had opened four paths in secret and believed Rei carried more than one. He read it twice. Then he went back to the chart in his head, the fourth factor, possession status at death, and to Gin's line about partial possession in the same chapter. The host is trapped, not gone. Not gone. That was the only path on any page that night that he was prepared to accept.
